# 18 — UI

Depends on: 10, 13, 14, 16, 17. Blocks: nothing.

## Decision gate

- Is `react-graph-vis` still the canvas? PolySim, the sibling project, runs it on React 19, which is the only reason it is the default over a hand-rolled SVG. If it breaks under Next 16, fall back to an adjacency list view first and a canvas later.
- Are routes still `/lectures`, `/lectures/[id]`, `/graph`, `/tutor`? They are the four surfaces this product has.

## Deliverables

```
src/app/lectures/page.tsx                  list, create
src/app/lectures/[id]/page.tsx             brief, sources, plan, review queue, publish
src/app/graph/page.tsx                     canvas plus link editor
src/app/tutor/page.tsx                     session
src/hooks/useLectures.ts, useReviewQueue.ts, useTutor.ts, useGraph.ts
src/lib/appRoutes.ts                       four new entries
src/i18n/messages/{en,de}.json             Lectures, Review, Graph, Tutor namespaces
```

## Lecture page

Four stacked sections, in the order a creator works:

1. **Brief** — a form over `lectures.brief`: audience, objectives (concept picker + verb select + depth text), mustCover, mustAvoid, duration, tone, language. Inline validation against the brief schema, no wizard.
2. **Sources** — a paste box and a Wikipedia search field with a candidate list (title, short description, licence, revision). One click adds a candidate. There is no file browser, no folder tree, no tagging. Sources are listed with licence and revision links because attribution has to be visible, not stored and forgotten.
3. **Plan** — visible after a creation job reaches `plan_ready`: one row per unit with concept, template, rationale, and the grounded sections; checkboxes to drop units. Editing the plan (removing units, swapping a template from the active list) is allowed and expected.
4. **Review queue** — the slop stop.

## The review queue

The highest-value screen in the product. Requirements, in priority order:

- **One act at a time, full width**, rendered as the learner would see it: title, steps with their roles, success criterion.
- **Grounding panel beside it**: the source sections the act was built from, un-truncated, with the source title and licence. This is what makes judging possible in seconds.
- **The template's rubric** as a checklist, unchecked by default. Not a gate — a prompt.
- **Two actions only**: accept, reject. Keyboard `a` and `r`, `j`/`k` to move between acts. No text box, no editor, no diff, no version history.
- **Grouping** by template, then by concept, with a count per group. Grouped review is the difference between 20 minutes and two hours.
- **Progress** "14 of 32 reviewed" and a filter for unreviewed only.
- Accepting a batch then publishing is one button, and the button explains what it will do in one sentence ("32 accepted, 0 proposed — publish lecture").

Rejection is silent afterwards: the act leaves the queue and stays rejected.

## Graph page

Concepts as nodes, `requires` as directed edges, `contrasts_with` as undirected, coloured by edge status. Click a node to see its acts (with template labels), its neighbours in both directions, and a link editor: pick a target concept and a type, submit. Cycle errors surface as the domain error, not as a failed request.

The act-to-concept edge is rendered as a label from the template key — this is where the vocabulary becomes visible to a user, so the labels must be the template names, not internal keys.

## Tutor page

A session with the act rendered step by step, a single answer field, and a "why this" panel that renders `turns.retrieval`: the seed scores, the traversal path with hop labels, and the component scores for the chosen act. The panel is not a debug tool behind a flag; it is the explanation of the product, and a learner who can see why an act was chosen can disagree with it.

Rehearsal mode shows the same screen with a banner and a "publish" shortcut.

## House rules that apply here

- New routes go into `APP_ROUTES` with `isMainNav` for the two primary ones; the navigation reads labels from `Nav` in both catalogues.
- No hardcoded UI text: `i18nScan.test.ts` fails the build. Every string lands in English and German, with matching placeholders.
- Empty states, loading states and error states come from `LoadingState`, `ErrorState` and `useErrorMessage`, which already exist.
- Mutations return rows; patch the react-query cache instead of refetching whole lists.
- Component tests follow the existing pattern: render with `renderWithIntl`, mock the tRPC hook, assert the interaction. At minimum: review accept, review reject via keyboard, plan unit removal, publish button disabled while proposed acts remain.

## Acceptance

- [~] **One** of four routes reachable from the sidebar: `/lectures` with English and German labels. `/tutor` and `/graph` do not exist yet, so they are deliberately absent from `APP_ROUTES` rather than linking to a 404.
- [x] The review queue can be worked end to end with the keyboard only — `a` accept, `r` reject, `j`/`k` move.
- [x] Accepting an act invalidates the act query, so the queue advances without a page reload.
- [ ] Publishing with one proposed act is disabled with an explanatory tooltip — **the button is not disabled**: the server refuses with `lectureNotPublishable` and the toast shows it. A disabled button without a reason is worse than a refusal with one; the tooltip version is open work.
- [ ] The "why this" panel — deferred with the tutor page.
- [x] Component tests for the review queue (4 tests), plus `npm run test:all` green including both i18n scans.

## State after execution

Built: `src/hooks/useLectures.ts`, `src/hooks/useReviewQueue.ts`, `/lectures` (list, create dialog), `/lectures/[id]` (tabs: review, plan, sources), `ReviewQueue`, `ReviewSidebar`, `PlanPanel`, `SourcePanel`, `labels.ts`, plus the `Lectures` and `Nav` catalogues in both languages.

Order chosen and why: the loop create → plan → review → publish is what makes the product usable, so lectures came first and the queue inside it. `/tutor` and `/graph` read what that loop produced; they are the next slice, not the first.

Deliberately not built yet, each with its reason:

- **the brief editor** — the most fiddly form in the product (objectives with verb and depth, mustCover/mustAvoid as concept pickers). `updateBrief` exists and is tested; the UI needs a concept picker backed by `concept.search`, which is a screen of its own. Until then a lecture's brief is set through the API.
- **the Wikipedia search panel** — `source.searchWiki` and `source.importWiki` exist; the panel is a listbox with a licence line per candidate.
- **`/tutor`** — needs the session loop wired to a chat surface plus the "why this" panel that renders `turns.retrieval`.
- **`/graph`** — needs the canvas decision (`react-graph-vis`), which the doc leaves open on purpose.

`@types/nextjs-routes.d.ts` is generated, but the generator only runs while the Next dev server is up, so `/lectures` and `/lectures/[id]` were added to it by hand in exactly the form the generator produces. Restarting the dev server overwrites the file identically; if the shapes ever diverge, the generator wins and `tsc` says so.

Two typing lessons worth keeping: `Link` to a dynamic route needs `route({ pathname, query })` from `nextjs-routes`, not a template string; and translated keys built from data (`t(\`rubricCodes.${code}\`)`) need a narrowing guard, which `labels.ts` now provides while falling back to the raw code so a new template without a translation shows its key instead of crashing.

## Anti-goals

- No act editor, no rich-text editing, no diff view, no comments on acts.
- No drag-and-drop plan reordering in the MVP; a number field or up/down buttons are enough.
- No mobile-specific layout work. The existing sidebar handles narrow screens reasonably.
- No marketing page, no onboarding tour. The tour infrastructure exists; using it is a later decision.
